name: Ramp
text: Add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page. This lets keyboard users bypass repetitive navigation blocks in one keystroke, cutting tab stops from dozens to one. The trade-off is a small visual footprint—one link—but it’s invisible to mouse users and doesn’t clutter the interface.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users still won’t notice the skip link—even with high contrast, it’s a single pixel-wide target that blends into the page’s rhythm. A better alternative is a skip link that’s both keyboard-visible and mouse-visible, positioned in the top-left corner with a persistent outline, settled by testing with actual keyboard users in a live prototype.

name: Ramp

Add a persistent skip link in the top-left corner with a high-contrast button that’s visible to both keyboard and mouse users. This guarantees sighted keyboard users won’t miss it while keeping the bypass option obvious for everyone. The trade-off is a small but permanent UI element—one that improves usability more than it clutters the interface.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is a persistent skip link in the top-left corner clutters the interface for sighted mouse users, especially on mobile where space is tight. A better alternative is a skip link that appears only on keyboard focus—high contrast, full-width, and triggered by Tab—then collapses when focus moves away. Settle it with user testing: measure if sighted keyboard users notice and use it, and if mouse users report visual noise.
